title: PAL firms up first Dreamliner order
summary: Flag carrier Philippine Airlines is adding up to 20 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners to its fleet, as it maximizes its international network for future growth.

blocks.text: Planes land and take off at Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Pasay City on March 23, 2026.
MANILA, Philippines — Flag carrier Philippine Airlines is adding up to 20 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners to its fleet, as it maximizes its international network for future growth.
In a signing, PAL entered into agreements with aerospace giant Boeing to buy 15 Dreamliners as was announced during the Farnborough International Airshow in July.
The agreements also cover the opportunity to purchase another five in the future, providing PAL with the flexibility to broaden its fleet as demand requires.
The 787-10, the largest member of the Dreamliner family, aims to boost PAL’s fleet upgrade. The aircraft will enable PAL to raise capacity for medium- and long-range flight.
Boeing committed to deliver the Dreamliner to PAL over the next decade. PAL will also become the first domestic carrier with a Dreamliner in its fleet, marking a new era for Philippine aviation.
PAL Holdings Inc. president and chief operating officer Lucio Tan III said the Dreamliner would enhance the airline’s fuel efficiency, given that the aircraft is equipped with new technologies.
“Its advanced technology, greater passenger capacity and improved fuel efficiency will also help us serve more passengers, improve our product offering and operate more efficiently,” Tan said.
The Dreamliner that PAL ordered would be powered by GE Aerospace’s GEnx-1B engines, one of the aviation industry’s most reliable mechanisms right now.
The Dreamliner is arguably the industry’s most popular aircraft because of its features. For one, the unit is the lightest and smoothest widebody jet, making long-range flights more comfortable.

Further, the 787-10 that PAL ordered is the biggest variant of the Dreamliner family, capable of flying between 300 and 375 passengers. The aircraft can fly as far as 13,890 kilometers and for PAL, this means reaching destinations across the Pacific Ocean.
Boeing also flexes the sustainability advantage of the Dreamliner, as it burns 25 percent less fuel compared to previous generations.
For passengers, the Dreamliner brings better comfort in its dimmable windows, higher humidity for dry air and reduced noise during turbulence.
